title: The First Annual Dungeon Dive Game Awards (2019)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I3T6O4ez75M

The first Dungeon Dive Game Awards, eight categories, bad news first. Biggest Disappointment goes to Skull Tales — a game Daniel (@dungeondive) expected to be his game of the year, undone by rules he calls a disaster and a developer response amounting to "our game is too complex for you." It stays on the shelf in hope someone reworks it.

The rest is enthusiasm. Biggest Surprise ties Explore! Forests of Adrimon (a Tom Chick review talked him past the drab iconography) with Cthulhu: Death May Die, which he expected to dislike on CMON principle and instead loved. Best Support is Blackstone Fortress, for a year of expansions from a company with a long history of abandoning its boxed games. Best Art is Dark Venture, praised for a singular creator's vision rather than mere competence. Most Underrated is *The Walking Dead: Here's Negan* — his least-viewed review of the year — for Negan moving independently as an agent of chaos, and a general plea for more NPCs like him.

The top five runs Call to Adventure, Adventure Games: The Dungeon, Core Space, Aeon's End: New Age, and Hellboy (Kickstarter version only — the retail box, he says, wouldn't make the list). Best experience of the year: finishing the Warhammer Quest playthrough series.

----

Is "most underrated" a useful award category, or just a reviewer flagging which of their own videos deserved more views?
